copy.title: How does frequency change sound pitch?
copy.tldr: Pitch sounds higher as the number of wave vibrations per second increases. Here f is frequency, λ is wavelength, v is the fixed sound speed of 343 m/s, and T is period; wavelength and period both decrease as frequency rises, but that does not mean the sound becomes louder.
copy.learning_objective: Explain causally how increasing sound-wave frequency creates a higher pitch while distinguishing pitch from loudness.
copy.misconception: A higher-frequency sound is not necessarily louder, but frequency determines pitch while amplitude determines loudness.
copy.explanation_prompt: Move the frequency and compare pitch with wavelength and period. Explain why both quantities decrease as pitch rises.
copy.transfer_prompt: Compare two equally loud sounds with different frequencies: which has the higher pitch, and how do their periods differ?
suggestions: Observe how period changes with frequency.
copy.brief_summary: Shows how frequency changes pitch, wavelength, and period without playing audio.
